# Codex 0.164.0 local `/status` output

Actual native Codex 0.164.0 ConPTY captures, recorded 2026-11-06 with the managed rendering argv `-c tui.disable_paste_burst=true` (default alternate screen is observed true). Each run has a fresh empty cwd, cleared inherited environment, separate HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA/XDG paths, short private CODEX_HOME, and a loopback Responses provider with `requires_openai_auth=false`. The provider emits fixed assistant text and no tool calls. No screenshot, real account/auth state, user session, external model, or user window was used. Session IDs in the status bodies were generated by these new isolated fixtures.

| Fixture | Before the status Enter | Observed action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status-manual` | Composer `/status`; menu still open, `/status` selected and `/statusline` also listed | Enter immediately executes `/status` |
| `status-menu-enter` | Composer `/st`; menu has selected `/status`, then `/statusline` and `/stop` | Enter immediately executes selected `/status`; no second Enter is needed |
| `status-tab-enter` | `/st` initially has the same menu; Tab changes composer to `/status` and closes the menu | Tab alone produces no status output; subsequent Enter executes `/status` |

Every scenario starts with an empty composer, submits `BKS_COMMAND32_FIRST`, receives response1, runs the explicit fixture status input, retains 2.6 seconds of actual quiet polls, submits `BKS_COMMAND32_SECOND`, receives response2, and exits naturally using `/quit`, code0.

`/status` produces a plain source echo `/status` **without `›`**, followed by `>_ OpenAI Codex`, Model, Model provider, Directory, Permissions, Agents.md, Collaboration mode, Session, Token usage, Context window, and Limits. This is local command output with no assistant bullet or new model-answer role. The active composer then returns to the empty `› Ask Codex to do anything` source state.

The status interval adds zero model requests: counters stay at one conversation POST plus one separate title POST. Each complete run has two conversation POSTs, two title POSTs, and two completed assistant responses. The title requests are not additional conversation answers.

Each `.vt` preserves every actual output byte. The matching JSON preserves every actual drain, including empty polls, input acceptance time, actual native wire bytes, separate logical input bytes, terminal protocol replies, and phase snapshots/cursors/mode/history. `command_contract.source_span` points into the actual `status-quiet.document_text` using UTF16 start/end offsets; it also records the corresponding VT range and explicit menu behavior. The `*-source.txt` files are exact extracted source spans, not rewritten examples.

Source intervals (UTF16 offsets in the recorded quiet document): manual `[110,681)`, Tab+Enter `[110,681)`, menu Enter `[110,729)`. Each quiet period contains 251 actual empty drains. Soft wrapping can join Directory/Permissions or Context/Limits into one logical line; tests should preserve the actual source rather than invent layout.

Raw launch/config/version/request/SSE/snapshot evidence and validation/owned-process cleanup receipts are under `target/codex-command32/`. Helper code is under `target/codex-production30/captures/helper/`; no shipping Rust or existing fixture was changed. These captures do not constitute a human NVDA test.
